summary: The note describes the Neighborhood Utility Upgrade Project (NUUP), a local government initiative announced September 15, 2023 under Mayor Evelyn K. Chambers to modernize aging water, sewage, power and gas infrastructure. It covers costs, jobs, smart grid and renewable plans, community education, and a phased rollout beginning December 2023. Officials argue upfront costs will be offset by avoided emergency repairs, efficiency gains and higher property values.
one_line: A local government's NUUP program overhauls aging water, sewer, power and gas utilities in phases, promising savings, jobs, smart grids and renewables.
key_facts: The initiative to overhaul aging utility infrastructure was announced starting September 15, 2023, led by Mayor Evelyn K. Chambers.
The Neighborhood Utility Upgrade Project (NUUP) covers water supply, sewerage, power, and gas.
City Engineer Jamal Peters said, "Our utilities are operating on borrowed time," warning of catastrophic failures without upgrades.

Finance committee chairperson Laura Higgs compared the upgrades to fixing a leaky roof, saying upfront costs are offset by preventing emergency repairs, improved efficiency, and higher property values.
The NUUP is expected to create jobs including construction workers, technicians, engineers, and support staff, and local contractors are incentivized to participate.
The project timeline is stated as five years with phased implementation, while the broader strategic plan covers the next decade.
Water conservation is a priority: old plumbing will be replaced and smart meters introduced to help residents monitor water usage.
Julie Benson, head of the local electricity board, aims to reduce blackout occurrences by 70% within the next two years via a smart grid.
Gas pipelines will be inspected and upgraded for safety and efficiency, and the sewage system will be upgraded to prevent overflows and protect public health.
The city is incentivizing homeowners to install solar panels and working to incorporate wind and solar farms into the grid.
Dr. Aaron Miller, a renewable energy expert, said the grid upgrade lays groundwork for a future powered mostly by clean, renewable sources.
The community education plan includes workshops, information sessions, and an interactive website; community liaison officer Rebecca Yu said informed residents make the transition smoother.
The first phase, starting in December 2023, will address the most critical areas identified by utility audits.
